The disbelievers' movement through the land is a small enjoyment ending in Hell, while those who feared their Lord abide forever in gardens beneath which rivers flow.
Those who disbelieve in Allah's verses burn in a Fire with their skins replaced, while believers who do righteous deeds abide forever in gardens with purified spouses.
Across a partition, the people of Paradise and of the Fire call to each other, the men on its elevations address both, and the Fire's people beg for water.
Those content with this world and heedless of the signs end in the Fire; righteous believers are in Gardens, glorifying Allah, greeting with peace, praising the Lord of the worlds.
Allah invites to the Home of Peace; those who do good have the best reward and more in Paradise; evildoers are repaid in kind, faces darkened, in the Fire forever.
The wretched will be in the Fire and the prosperous in Paradise, each abiding as long as the heavens and earth endure, except what the Lord wills.
Disbelievers face punishment in this world and worse in the Hereafter; the Paradise promised to the righteous has rivers, lasting fruit and shade, while the disbelievers' end is the Fire.
Those taken in death while wronging themselves will enter the gates of Hell, while the righteous, greeted by the angels with peace at death, enter Paradise.
Truth is from your Lord, so let whoever wills believe or disbelieve; wrongdoers face fire and scalding drink, while believers who do good have gardens, gold bracelets and silk.
Disbelievers and what they worship besides Allah will be fuel for Hell, while those promised the best are far from it, untroubled by the greatest terror and welcomed by angels.
Two adversaries dispute over their Lord, a verse revealed about the duel at Badr: disbelievers get garments of fire, scalding water and iron maces, believers wear gold, pearl and silk.
Those who deny the Hour face a roaring Blaze, chained in a narrow place crying for destruction, while the righteous are promised the Garden of Eternity with whatever they wish.
Believers who did righteous deeds will be delighted in a garden, while those who disbelieved and denied the verses and the Hereafter will be brought into punishment.
None can save one deserving punishment in the Fire, while those who feared their Lord have chambers built high above chambers, with rivers flowing beneath, Allah's promise.
Disbelievers will be driven in groups to Hell and the God-fearing in groups to Paradise, which they enter praising Allah, while angels surround the Throne exalting their Lord.
Believers enter gardens while disbelievers eat like livestock and dwell in the Fire; stronger cities were destroyed; Paradise's rivers of water, milk, wine and honey are set against scalding water.
Hell is asked if it is full and asks for more, while Paradise is brought near to the righteous who returned to Allah, entering in peace with whatever they wish.
Every soul is held for its deeds except the companions of the right, who ask criminals what put them in Saqar: no prayer, no feeding the poor, idle talk, denial.
When the great Calamity comes and Hellfire is exposed, whoever transgressed and preferred worldly life goes to Hellfire, and whoever feared his Lord and restrained his desires goes to Paradise.
The righteous will be in pleasure and the wicked in Hellfire, burning there on the Day of Recompense and never absent from it.
Whoever gets his record in his right hand has an easy account and returns happy; whoever gets it behind his back burns, having thought he would never return.
